attention.message: IT HAS NOW HAPPENED TWICE, so this is a pattern and not an accident. The 2026-09-02 run generated data/status.json (generatedAt 06:33:13Z) and index.html, then never committed, never pushed and never appended to data/history.ndjson — exactly as the 2026-08-31 run did. Verified this morning: the 09-02 build was still sitting uncommitted in the working tree, the last commit on main was 2026-09-01 18:20, and the last journal line is 2026-09-01T16:20Z. The public dashboard therefore served 09-01 data for two days, twice in four days, with no alarm of any kind. The watcher is failing at the precise shape it exists to catch: it fires, it produces, and it publishes nothing. Its own freshness rule measures the COMMIT, so it does eventually self-flag — but only as a yellow, and only two days late.

fix.prompt: In ~/AI eksperimenter/Routine overview: the secretary run has now silently skipped its publish step twice (2026-08-31 and 2026-09-02) — both runs wrote data/status.json and index.html, then never committed, pushed or journalled, and the dashboard served stale data for two days each time with no alarm. Fix the class, not the instance. (1) Move the journal append BEFORE the publish step so a crash between the two is visible in history.ndjson rather than invisible. (2) After pushing, assert that the committed data/status.json at HEAD has the same generatedAt as the one just produced, and fail loudly if not. (3) Add a self-check the NEXT run performs: if the newest history.ndjson entry is older than one scheduler period, treat that as a red publish-failure automatically instead of relying on a human noticing. Edit routines/secretary-hourly.md and the scheduled task at ~/.claude/scheduled-tasks/routine-overview-secretary/SKILL.md. Verify by simulating a failed push and confirming the next run reports it.

attention.message: FOURTH FLAG, and today is the cleanest proof yet that it is the fleet's single point of failure. Both editions published on time — Alexanders Brief 04:32Z = 06:32 CPH, Thomas' Nyheder 04:45Z = 06:45 CPH — and BOTH came from com.abustrup.brief-cloud-trigger's 05:56 dispatch. GitHub delivered zero event=schedule runs to either repo today as of 08:38 CPH; yesterday its own crons did fire but not until 10:43-11:37 CPH, hours past the 08:00 deadline. Nothing on this board watches the only job that meets the deadline. AND IT LOGGED ITS FIRST FAILURE TODAY — with a caveat that matters more than the failure: trigger.log records 'FAILED to dispatch abustrup/thomas-nyheder' at 06:20:28, but GitHub shows that dispatch DID create a successful run at 03:56:16Z. The gh call hung ~24 minutes and returned non-zero after the API had already accepted the request. So the log's own failure line is wrong, and that log is the artifact any enrolment would read.

fix.prompt: In ~/AI eksperimenter/Routine overview, config/projects.json: add a routine row for the launchd job com.abustrup.brief-cloud-trigger — id 'brief-cloud-trigger', project 'news-brief', kind 'launchd', role 'producer', enabled true, cadence '05:45 & 08:30', periodHours 24, freshness {type:'logMtime', path:'{HOME}/.brief-ci/trigger.log'}. CRITICAL, verified 2026-09-03: do NOT make 'FAILED to dispatch' an error pattern on its own. That exact line appeared today for thomas-nyheder while the dispatch had actually SUCCEEDED (run created 2026-09-03T03:56:16Z, conclusion success) — ~/.brief-ci/trigger-cloud.sh logs FAILED whenever `gh workflow run` returns non-zero, and gh hung 24 minutes and exited non-zero after GitHub had already accepted the call. An enrolment keyed on that string would produce false reds. Either treat FAILED as a warn, or make the check verify against `gh api repos/<r>/actions/runs` that a run was created within the hour. The genuinely fatal signatures are 'FAILED: gh not on PATH' and 'FAILED: gh not authenticated', which abort before either repo is fired. Also add rows for dagens-kompas-daily, harness-review and prompt-library-review, unenrolled for 11 consecutive runs. Then node scripts/collect.mjs && node scripts/render.mjs, verify the cards render, commit and push.
